transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess… I just haven’t been wanting to do much of anything lately. Things I used to look forward to—salsa nights, church stuff, cooking for folks nearby… even going into my shop just to smell the wood. I don’t really feel pulled toward any of it now.
Did this start after something stressful happened in your life?
Yeah… I think so. It’s been about two months now, since my wife’s health kind of suddenly got worse and our routine changed. That’s when I started noticing I wasn’t acting like myself.
If your wife’s health had not worsened, do you think you would still be feeling this loss of interest?

I don’t know. Maybe… maybe not. What I do know is I’ve stopped wanting to do the things that usually keep me steady—salsa, church gatherings, cooking for neighbors… even going into my shop just to smell the wood. It’s just not there right now.
Do you feel this loss of interest is mainly because of your wife’s health worsening?

Maybe partly… I don’t know. What I know is I’ve stopped wanting to do the things that usually keep me going—salsa, church gatherings, cooking for neighbors… even just walking into my shop to smell the wood. It’s all kind of gone quiet.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most days?
Yeah… most days. Especially in the morning. I wake up with this heavy, empty feeling in my chest, and I have to kind of hold it together so I don’t break down in front of my wife.
Have these feelings been making it hard for you to manage your usual daily responsibilities?

Yeah… it has. I’ve had to let other guys take over parts of jobs I’d normally watch myself. And I’ve kind of stopped showing up for people—church, friends, neighbors. It got bad enough that my wife and someone from the parish got worried about me.
Have you had thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself?

Yeah… I’ve had thoughts like that. Not so much… I don’t know… not wanting to say it out loud. Sometimes I think maybe it’d be easier if I just didn’t wake up. And then I catch myself thinking my family might be better off without me.

That scares me.
Have you thought about how you might kill yourself?
Not… not in a specific way, no. It’s more like I think maybe it’d be easier if I didn’t wake up, or that my family might be better off without me. And then I get scared that I’m even thinking that.
Before this started two months ago, have you ever had another period in your life when you felt depressed like this for days or weeks at a time?
I guess… I’m not sure about before, but this time it’s been going on longer than two months. More like… six months. It doesn’t feel like just a rough week or regular stress anymore.
When you have a moment away from your wife’s health situation, does the depressed feeling still stay with you?

Yeah. It’s still there.

Even when nothing is happening right that second… most mornings I wake up with this heavy, empty feeling. Like the whole house has gone gray, and I’m just trying to keep it together so my wife doesn’t see me fall apart.
Before this current stretch, have you ever had another period in your life when you felt depressed most days for at least two weeks?
I… I don’t really know. Nothing like this that I can clearly point to. Maybe I’ve had low times, but… not something I can say was most days for two weeks.
Have you been feeling worthless?

Yeah… I have.

I keep going over everything with my wife—appointments, little changes I missed—and I tell myself maybe if I’d been a better husband, I would’ve caught it sooner or somehow protected her.
Have you been having trouble with sleep lately?

I’m not really sure how to answer that.

I mean… sleep hasn’t felt normal, I guess, but I haven’t been keeping track of it. Some nights are just… harder than others.
Have you had a noticeable change in your appetite lately?
I don’t know… I haven’t really been paying attention to it. Maybe a little different, but nothing I can say for sure.
Before this started getting worse, had you already been feeling down or low most days for at least two years?
I’m not sure. I don’t think I’ve really looked at it that way… it’s hard to say what was “most days” over that long.
Before this current period, was there ever another time in your life when you felt depressed nearly every day for at least two weeks?
I don’t know… maybe. I’ve had rough stretches before, but I can’t really say if it was nearly every day for two weeks. I didn’t keep track like that.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?

Yeah… some. I’ll be looking at blueprints I’ve read my whole life, and it’s like the lines just sort of blur together in my head. I end up asking the younger guys to repeat things I should’ve caught the first time.
Before this current period, was there ever a time in your life when you felt depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks?
I… I don’t know about before this. Lately it’s most mornings I wake up with this heavy, empty feeling, like all the color’s gone out of the house. I try not to fall apart in front of my wife.
Before this current episode, were there two years in a row when you felt down or depressed most days?
I don’t think so… not two years like that. I’ve had bad patches, but I couldn’t say it was most days for that long.
Before this current period, was there ever a time when you lost interest in almost everything for at least two weeks?

Yeah… I mean, that’s kind of what brought me in now. I stopped wanting to do the things that usually keep me going — salsa nights, church stuff, cooking for the neighbors. Even going into my shop just to smell the wood… I don’t really want to.
